NONE: › to swear, using words that are considered offensive
講粗話；罵人
› something that is said in order to tell someone rudely to go away
滾蛋！滾開！

T: › [ T ] formal to remove something intentionally

NONE: › to behave in a modest way and treat the good things that you have achieved as if they are not important, often because you do not have much confidence
保持低調；使自己不被人注意；不露鋒芒

example: The whole country had tried to efface the memory of the old dictatorship.
整個國家都曾試圖將那段獨裁歷史從記憶中抹去。
See also
self-effacing

C or U: B1 [ C or U ] the result of a particular influence
C1 to produce or achieve the results you want
› If you say or do something for effect, you intentionally do it to shock people or attract their attention.
C2 in fact, or in practice
› used to express that what you are reporting is only a short and general form of what was really said
有…的意思；大意是…，意思是…

NONE: B1 lighting, sounds, and objects that are specially produced for the stage or a film and are intended to make something that does not exist seem real
特技效果
› a person's possessions, especially after their death
（尤指死後遺留的）財産，財物，所有物
› to achieve something and cause it to happen
使發生；實現；完成

example: The radiation leak has had a disastrous effect on/upon the environment.
核輻射外泄給環境帶來了災難性的影響。
I tried taking tablets for the headache but they didn't have any effect.
我試著吃了幾顆藥片，但頭痛一點都沒有減輕。
I think I'm suffering from the effects of too little sleep.
我覺得我睡眠太少，健康受到了影響。
She has a lot of confidence, which she uses to good effect (= to her advantage) in interviews.
她很自信，在面試時她充分利用這一點，佔盡了優勢。
See also
aftereffects
They had to wait ten minutes for the anaesthetic to take effect before they stitched up the cut.
他們不得不等了十分鐘，在麻醉藥起作用後才縫合傷口。
I get the impression that she uses bad language in meetings for effect.
我覺得她開會時說髒話是在故意引人注意。
So in effect the government have lowered taxes for the rich and raised them for the poor.
所以呢，實際上政府是為富人減了稅，而給窮人加了稅。
She said she was unhappy, or words to that effect.
她說了一些她很不幸福之類的話。
He said something to the effect that he would have to change jobs if the situation continued.
他話裡的意思是說，如果這種情況再持續下去，他將不得不換個工作。
The present system of payment will remain in effect (= be used) until the end of the rental agreement.
在租期結束前，將會繼續採用現行的付款方式。
When do the new driving laws come into effect?
新的道路交通安全法規甚麽時候開始實施？
The new salary increases will take effect (= begin) from January onwards.
新的加薪標準將從一月份起正式實行。
This is a movie worth seeing for its effects alone.
這部電影光憑其特技效果就值得一看。
It says on the form that the insurance covers all personal effects.
表上寫明，所有個人財產都在該保險承保範圍之內。
As a political party they are trying to effect a change in the way that we think about our environment.
作為一個政治黨派，他們正在試圖改變我們關於環境的觀念。

NONE: B2 successful or achieving the results that you want
能産生預期結果的；有效的

before noun: › [ before noun ] in fact, although not officially

NONE: › If a law or rule becomes effective, it starts to be used.
（法律法規）生效的

example: It's an extremely effective cure for a headache.
這種藥物治療頭痛極其有效。
The lighting for the production made a very effective use of shadow.
該戲劇的舞臺燈光設計巧妙地運用了陰影效果。
She's a very effective teacher.
她課教得非常好。
Opposite
ineffective
Although she's not officially our boss, she's in effective control of the office.
她雖然名義上不是我們的老闆，但實際上掌管著該辦事處。
The new laws will become effective next month.
新法律將在下月正式生效。

NONE: B2 in a way that is successful and achieves what you want
有效地
C2 used when you describe what the real result of a situation is
實際上；事實上

example: The tablets work more effectively if you take a hot drink after them.
服用這些藥片後再喝杯熱飲，藥效會更好。
His wife left him when the children were small, so he effectively brought up the family himself.
在孩子還很小的時候妻子就離開了他，所以實際上是他一手把孩子們撫養長大的。
Effectively, we have to start again from scratch.
實際情況是，我們不得不重新從零開始。

NONE: › a body part or cell that reacts to a stimulus in a particular way, or a cell or substance in the body that produces an effect
效應器，效應物（生物中對刺激作出反應的身體部分、細胞或物質）

example: In a reflex, the effector muscle acts before your brain is able to think.
做反射動作時，效應肌肉在大腦還沒有思考時就作出了反應。

NONE: › effective and successful
卓有成效的，有效的；奏效的

example: They wish to promote a real and effectual understanding between the two countries.
他們希望真正有效地促進兩國間的理解。

NONE: › An effeminate man behaves or looks similar to a woman.
（男人）女人氣的，女性化的，沒有男子漢氣概的

example: He's got a very effeminate manner/voice.
他舉止／說話很娘娘腔。

NONE: › away from a central organ or part
（從主要器官或身體部位）傳出的，輸出的；離心的

example: An efferent nerve carries signals away from the brain and spinal cord.
傳出神經將信號從大腦和脊髓中傳出。

NONE: › If a liquid effervesces, it produces small bubbles.
冒泡；起沫；泡騰
› An effervescent liquid produces bubbles of gas.
冒泡的；起沫的；泡騰的
› active, positive, and full of energy
充滿活力的；活潑的；興高采烈的

example: She's one of those effervescent personalities that you often see hosting TV game shows.
她是那種很會活躍氣氛人，常常主持電視競賽節目。

NONE: › literary disapproving weak and without much power
弱不禁風的；了無生氣的；軟弱無能的
› disapproving more typical of a woman than of a man
沒有男子漢氣概的；女人氣的

example: With nothing to do all day the aristocracy had grown effete and lazy.
貴族們終日無所事事，變得四體不勤，懶散乏力。

NONE: › able to produce the intended result
靈驗的；奏效的；有效的
› the ability, especially of a medicine or a method of achieving something, to produce the intended result
功效，效力，效能

example: They recently ran a series of tests to measure the efficacy of the drug.
他們最近進行了一系列的試驗來檢測這種藥的功效。
Synonym
effectiveness

NONE: B2 the good use of time and energy in a way that does not waste any
效率；效能；功效
› specialized physics the difference between the amount of energy that is put into a machine in the form of fuel, effort, etc. and the amount that comes out of it in the form of movement
（機器的）功率

example: What is so impressive about their society is the efficiency of the public services.
他們的社會給人留下最深刻印象的是其高效率的公共服務。
energy efficiency
能源使用效率

NONE: B1 working or operating quickly and effectively in an organized way
效率高的；有能力的；有效的；生效的

example: The city's transport system is one of the most efficient in Europe.
這座城市的交通系統運行效率很高，在全歐洲名列前茅。
We need someone really efficient who can organize the office and make it run smoothly.
我們需要的人必須要高效幹練，善於組織籌劃，能使這個辦事處順暢運作。

NONE: › a model or other object that represents someone, especially one of a hated person that is hanged or burned in a public place
（尤指被憎恨人的）模擬像，雕像；畫像：

example: Crowds marched through the streets carrying burning effigies of the president.
示威群眾舉著燃燒的總統畫像沿街遊行。

NONE: › used to add force to an expression. Some people might consider this offensive
（用於加強語氣，具有冒犯性）該死的

example: He's such an effing nuisance!
他真的是煩死人了！

NONE: › the use of gentle, circular hand movements in massage (= rubbing or pressing someone's body to relax them or reduce pain)
按撫法（按摩手法，手掌重複性地做環形按摩）
› specialized biology the period when flowers start to appear on a plant
開花；開花期
› literary the production of a lot of art, especially of a high quality
（藝術等的）發展，繁榮；（尤指藝術等發展的）全盛期
› liquid waste that is sent out from factories or places where sewage is dealt with, usually flowing into rivers, lakes, or the sea
廢水，污水

example: Effluents from local factories are finding their way into the river.
當地工廠排出的廢水都任其流入河中。

C or U: B1 [ C or U ] physical or mental activity needed to achieve something
C: › [ C ] the result of an attempt to produce something, especially when its quality is low or uncertain
（尤指不理想的或難以確定的）結果
C2 to be difficult, tiring, or boring to do

example: [ + to infinitive ] If we could all make an effort to keep this office tidier it would help.
如果我們都努力保持整潔，那麽辦公室的面貌肯定會大有改觀。
You can't expect to have any friends if you don't make the effort with people.
如果不努力去和人們交往，你就別想有朋友。
In their efforts to reduce crime the government expanded the police force.
爲了減少犯罪，政府擴充了警力。
He's jogging around the park every morning in an effort to get fit.
爲了調整好身體狀況，他現在每天早晨都繞著公園慢跑。
It takes a long time to prepare the dish but the results are so good that it's worth the effort.
做這道菜很費時間，但結果大家都很愛吃，工夫真沒白費。
Do you want to have a look at his exam paper? It's a fairly poor effort.
你想看看他的試卷嗎？成績可不太好。
I'm exhausted all the time, and everything is a real effort.
我總是覺得精疲力盡，無論做什麼都很費勁。

NONE: › seeming not to need any effort
不費力的；輕鬆的

example: When you watch her dance it looks so effortless.
她的舞姿看上去非常輕盈。
He was an actor of effortless charm.
他是位瀟灑自如、魅力十足的演員。

NONE: › extreme rudeness without any ability to understand that your behaviour is not acceptable to other people
厚顔無恥；放肆

example: He was silent all through the meal and then had the effrontery to complain that I looked bored!
在飯桌上他自始至終一言不發，到頭來卻有臉抱怨我一副百無聊賴的樣子。

NONE: › shining brightly: an effulgent canopy of stars
› looking very beautiful or full of goodness: her effulgent beauty an effulgent smile
› a sudden and uncontrolled expression of strong emotion
（強烈感情的）迸發，傾瀉

example: an effusion of anger and despair
突然陷入憤怒和絕望之中

NONE: › expressing welcome, approval, or pleasure in a way that shows very strong feeling
熱情的，熱情洋溢的；奔放的

example: They gave us such an effusive welcome it was quite embarrassing.
他們的歡迎儀式搞得如此熱烈，倒讓我們頗有些不好意思。
